--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.condensation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Collapse each strongly connected component into a single node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.condensation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Collapse each strongly connected component into a single node. title: >- [Graph.condensation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Collapse each strongly connected component into a single node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Collapse each strongly connected component into a single node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58090-L58187){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.condensation() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Condensation](/assets/graphs/condensation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed graph whose strongly connected components are shaded: the cycle A, B, C (accent color), the two-way pair D, E (teal), and the single nodes F (violet) and G (gold). Right: the condensation has one node per component, labeled {A,B,C}, {D,E}, F and G, joined by the edges that ran between components, {A,B,C} to {D,E} and F to G; the result is acyclic." width="100%"} A strongly connected component (SCC) is a maximal group of nodes that can all reach one another. Replacing each SCC with one node, and keeping an edge between two components whenever any edge ran between their members, gives the *condensation*: a directed acyclic graph that shows the large-scale flow of the network once its cycles are folded away. It is the standard first step for applying DAG methods (topological order, longest paths, ancestors) to a graph that has cycles. Each node of the result carries: - a `label`: the original label for a single-node component, or the member labels in braces for a larger one, e.g. `"{A,B,C}"` - `members`: the list of member labels - `size`: the number of members Components are added in topological order, so following the new node IDs in increasing order never goes against an edge. Parallel edges between the same two components are merged into one. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new directed acyclic graph. The original graph is not modified. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two cycles joined by a one-way edge condense into a two-node DAG, and the isolated node E becomes a component of its own: ::: {#206f0c52 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "C")]) ) dag = graph.condensation() dag.get_node_df().select(["id", "label", "members", "size"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
